title: Regime-Dependent Validity in Energy-Flow Cosmology: Evidence from SPARC Galaxy Rotation Curves and the EFC-R Framework
description: Pilot-scale empirical test of Energy-Flow Cosmology (EFC) on 20 SPARC galaxies spanning LSB, dwarf irregular, spiral, and barred/disturbed morphologies. The study finds regime-dependent validity—EFC excels in low-complexity systems (LSB, diffuse dwarfs) and underperforms in structurally complex galaxies—motivating the EFC-R meta-framework with the decomposition E_total = E_flow + E_latent.
author: Morten Magnusson

effective_energy_field.description: Defines the effective energy field in EFC as local energy density ρ suppressed by a normalized entropy field S ∈ [0,1].

rotation_velocity.description: Circular velocity predicted from the radial derivative of the effective energy-flow potential Φ_eff.

delta_AIC.description: Model comparison metric: negative values favor EFC; positive values favor ΛCDM.

regime_decomposition.description: EFC-R meta-framework decomposition separating flow-governed and latent (structural/non-equilibrium) contributions.

key_results.main_finding: EFC shows regime-dependent validity: competitive or preferred in 80% of the 20-galaxy SPARC pilot (especially LSB/diffuse dwarfs), with performance degrading in structurally complex (barred/disturbed) systems; EFC fits exhibit a significant correlation with a latent-field complexity proxy (Spearman ρ = 0.705, p = 0.0005).

sealed_predictions.statement: On an expanded SPARC-like sample (N > 100), the EFC success rate (ΔAIC ≤ 2 vs ΛCDM) will be significantly higher for low-L (low-complexity) galaxies—LSB and diffuse dwarfs—than for high-L (barred/disturbed) systems.
sealed_predictions.falsifiable_by: Compute ΔAIC per galaxy on a preregistered, enlarged sample and test for a statistically significant difference in success rates between low-L and high-L subsets.

sealed_predictions.statement: The latent field proxy L will positively correlate with EFC misfit (e.g., ΔAIC or χ2_red difference) with Spearman ρ ≳ 0.5 at p < 0.01 on larger samples after bootstrap resampling.
sealed_predictions.falsifiable_by: Estimate L and EFC performance metrics for a larger, quality-controlled sample and evaluate Spearman ρ with uncertainty via bootstrap.

sealed_predictions.statement: In dynamically relaxed LSB galaxies (low L), best-fit entropy gradients ∇S will cluster around the reported mean (∼8.20×10^-2 kpc^-1) with modest scatter (≈2.44×10^-2 kpc^-1).
sealed_predictions.falsifiable_by: Fit EFC to a larger LSB subset and test whether the ∇S distribution mean and scatter match the reported values within uncertainties.

kill_criteria: KC1: In an expanded, high-quality SPARC sample (N ≥ 100) with uniform mass modeling, ≤ 30% of low-complexity galaxies (LSB/diffuse dwarfs) yield ΔAIC ≤ 2 for EFC (binomial p < 0.01 versus the pilot’s ~80% rate).

KC2: The latent field proxy L shows no robust positive correlation with EFC misfit on a larger sample (|ρ| ≤ 0.2 with p ≥ 0.1 after bootstrap and controls), contradicting the reported ρ = 0.705 (p = 0.0005).

KC3: Physically invalid entropy solutions are systematically required in low-complexity systems: S outside [0,1] or widespread sign-inconsistent ∇S across radii in ≥ 20% of relaxed LSB/diffuse dwarfs with high-quality data.

KC4: In a preregistered analysis of structurally complex (barred/disturbed) galaxies, introducing an E_latent term (EFC-R) fails to improve penalized fit quality (AIC/BIC) over base EFC in ≥ 70% of cases.

KC5: Across regimes, reduced chi-squared systematically favors ΛCDM by a large margin (e.g., χ2_red,ΛCDM − χ2_red,EFC ≤ 0 or > +5 in the majority of low-complexity galaxies) when using the same baryonic inputs and error models.
name: EFC-R-SPARC-Regime-Validity
abstract: We analyze 20 galaxies from the SPARC database using the EFC framework, finding systematic patterns in where EFC succeeds versus fails. We develop EFC-R (Regime): a meta-framework that operationalizes regime-dependent validity through the decomposition E_total = E_flow + E_latent.
